title.narrative: Provision of Multi-Sector life Saving Response for vulnerable populations affected at Oromia Region Borena Zone, Moyale and Dubuluk Woredas

description.narrative:
ltpgtltp style="text-align:justifyline-height:107%" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family:"gtTo address the emergency needs of IDPs and host communities at lt/spangtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif"gtMoyale and Dubuluk Woredas of Borean Zone,lt/spangtltspan style="font-family:"gt lt/spangtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif"gtAAH partnering with Gayo Pastoralist Development Initiative – GPDI (local implementing partner) designed Multi-sector humanitarian response compromising Cash Assistance, Agriculture, WASH, a Protection. lt/spangtltspan style="font-family:"gtIt is believed Cash Assistance will support the targeted households to fill their most critical needs. Through Cash Assistance, AAH will distribute 6,900 ETB ($128) in one round per household total of 20,700 ETB ($383.37) in three rounds to cover set of basic recurring needs. 11,840,400 ETB ($219,286.12) will be distributed to 572 households or 2860 (F: 1459, M: 1401) individuals in 3 rounds. The transfer value is set based on interim guidance for the Oromia Region recommended by Ethiopian Cash Working Group. Beneficiary targeting is based on AAH’s Cash SOP. Beneficiary targeting selection process carried out with respective government offices community representatives. Registration will be undertaken using lt/spangtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif"gtRed Roselt/spangtltspan style="font-family:"gt beneficiary profile registration tool. Biometric devices will be used and fingerprints of each target beneficiary will be collected. Biometric data will be used as identifier of registered beneficiary. AAH will work with Awash Bank. GPDI provides Agricultural inputs (Seeds and farm tools) for Agro–pastoralist farmers whose livelihood have been negatively affected The agricultural inputs are Teff and haircoat bean which is required by the community. The project will also provide farm tools like digging hoe and sickles along with the seeds. The seeds are distributed based on local seeds rates that each woreda Agriculture, Livestock and Rural Development offices recommend based on the existing soil type and agro ecology of each location. Pastoralist communities will be supported through the supply of livestock vaccines and livestock health treatment activities. This will protect the losses of the core livestock of drought-affected communities, contribute to maintain the body condition of animals, and support milk production for the families. Livestock mass vaccination campaigns and treatment activities will result in the vaccination and treatment of a minimum 28,000 (8,000 cattle, 20,000 goats sheep) heads of livestock. Small ruminants as restocking activity will be provided. Local species goats will distributed to most vulnerable pastoralist communities. The small ruminants will be distributed to those families who have completely lost their livestock. Priority will be given to pregnant and lactating women and women headed households. Through this action, 1648 Goats will be distributed to 410 households (2050 individuals). Beneficiary targeting will be done with close collaboration from government counterparts and representatives from both IDPs and host communities. ltbrgtltbrgtltbrgt
lt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="margin-bottom:9.95pt" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family:"gtltspan style="font-size:8.0pt mso-bidi-font-size:10.0ptfont-family:"gtEmergency WASH response address immediate lifesaving needs of the drought affected community through provision of lifesaving WASH NFI water treatment products at household level, hygiene and sanitation promotion, installation of emergency sanitation services water facilities at community level will be done by AAH. The project foresees to build resilience through implementation of durable solution. lt/spangtltspan style="font-size:8.0ptmso-bidi-font-size:10.0ptfont-family:"gtProtection response by AAH will focus on the key emergency priorities for a protection program that responds to the needs of survivors of violence and abuse. Program activities will strengthen and support GBV systems to respond to cases of GBV/IPV survivors and those at risk, provision of MHPSS for both a response and mitigation approach, increasing the capacity of key government workers through training and on-going support (including case management), improving and strengthening of safe referral systems, inclusion of key stakeholders and local communities in creating risk mitigation awareness, provision of dignity kits for the most vulnerable and support, training and partnership with a local disability charity.lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="sceditor-nlf"gtltbrgtlt/pgtlt/pgt
